The page describes an Energy Star certified, LEED Silver certified campus with seismic protection for customer equipment and on site EV charging.

reading.body:
QTS Santa Clara 2 publishes 7.5 MW of IT capacity across a multi-building campus on Mission College Boulevard in Santa Clara, California, though the operator does not separately specify which buildings comprise this facility or break out distinct capacity figures between Santa Clara 1 and Santa Clara 2.

At 40 kW per rack, a density typical of AI training workloads, 7.5 MW supports roughly 188 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a colocation baseline, it supports roughly 750 racks. These are calculations based on assumed rack density, not operator claims about actual configuration. The campus holds Energy Star and LEED Silver certification, meaning it meets recognized standards for energy efficiency in construction and operation. The operator page publishes no uptime tier, power redundancy specification, or connectivity detail.

Among 103 mapped facilities in California, only seven publish a megawatt figure. QTS Santa Clara 2 ranks fourth among those seven, representing roughly 4 percent of the 185 MW this site has recorded statewide. This ranking is fragile. The gap between mapped facilities and those with published data means the true California total is almost certainly larger, and this facility's standing could shift significantly as more operators disclose capacity.

For AI workload evaluation, 7.5 MW is moderate by current hyperscale standards, where single training clusters regularly consume tens of megawatts or more. LEED certification addresses building efficiency and environmental design, not the power delivery density or fiber connectivity that AI clusters depend on most. Whether this campus hosts GPU clusters, how its power architecture is designed, or how it connects to the grid remain unpublished, requiring direct operator inquiry.
